name: Ala Moana Center
description: Hawaii's largest open-air shopping center (350+ stores). Luxury to local brands, huge food court (Makai Market), and direct access to Ala Moana Beach Park.

name: Royal Hawaiian Center
description: Waikiki's premier shopping — 3 levels, 110+ stores. Free cultural programming daily: hula lessons, lei making, ukulele, Hawaiian quilting.

name: Waikele Premium Outlets
description: 50+ designer outlets (Coach, Kate Spade, Nike, etc.) ~30 min from Waikiki. Best for brand discounts. Tourist bus groups common on weekends.

name: International Market Place
description: Open-air Waikiki center under a massive banyan tree. Mix of local artisans, global brands, and dining. Heritage-themed design.

name: KCC Farmers Market
address: 4303 Diamond Head Rd (Kapiolani CC parking lot)
description: Oahu's BEST farmers market (Saturdays only). Local produce, prepared foods, poke, malasadas, Vietnamese, Hawaiian plates. Pair with early Diamond Head hike.

name: Chinatown Markets
address: N King St & Kekaulike St / 1120 Maunakea St
description: Oahu Market (open-air, oldest) + Maunakea Marketplace (indoor food court). Fresh fish, char siu, exotic produce, cheap local eats. Best in morning.

name: Kahala Mall
description: Upscale neighborhood mall (Whole Foods, Macy's, local boutiques). Quieter than Ala Moana. Good Whole Foods for picnic supplies.

name: Ward Village / Kaka'ako
description: Master-planned neighborhood with SALT, Ward Centre, Ward Village Shops. Local designers, art galleries, weekend farmers market, great coffee (Brue Bar).

name: Dole Plantation
description: Tourist-heavy but fun stop en route to North Shore. Pineapple garden maze, train ride, famous Dole Whip. Gift shop with pineapple everything.

name: Helena's Hawaiian Food
description: James Beard Award winner. THE traditional Hawaiian spot since 1946. Pipikaula (dried salted short rib), lau lau, poi, haupia. Cash only, lunch only, arrive before 11AM.

name: Ono Hawaiian Foods
description: Kapahulu institution since 1963. Kalua pig, lau lau, lomi salmon, opihi (seasonal). Cash only, walk-in. Walkable from Waikiki.

name: Rainbow Drive-In
description: Obama's go-to plate lunch since 1961. Mixed plate (~$12): 2-scoop rice, mac salad + entrée. Loco moco, chili rice, saimin. Iconic.

name: Leonard's Bakery
description: THE malasada spot since 1952. Portuguese fried dough, hot, rolled in sugar. Original $1.50–2. Filled (custard, haupia) $2.25–2.75. Walk 10 min from Waikiki.

name: Marukame Udon
description: Handmade udon made fresh on-site. Cafeteria-style. Kake udon ~$4, tempura udon, fresh-fried tempura from counter. Always a line, moves fast. Best budget meal in Waikiki.

name: Yama's Fish Market
description: Top-tier poke source. Locals shop here daily. Ahi shoyu, spicy ahi, kimchi poke, tako. Buy by pound or bowl. Not a sit-down restaurant.

name: Foodland Farms Ala Moana
description: Supermarket with legendary poke counter inside Ala Moana Center. Get Maika'i loyalty card at register (free, no residency needed) for instant discounts.

name: Tamura's Fine Wine & Liquors
description: Liquor store with a legendary poke counter — only in Hawaii. Furikake ahi is exceptional. Multiple locations (Aiea, Kaimuki, Hawaii Kai).

name: Cinnamon's Restaurant
description: Voted best breakfast on Oahu. Guava chiffon pancakes, macadamia nut French toast. In Kailua — pair with Kailua Beach. Reserve weekends.

name: Boots & Kimo's
description: Legendary macadamia nut pancakes with sweet white sauce. Walk-in only, line forms early. Loco moco also great. Kailua.

name: Koko Head Cafe
description: Chef Lee Anne Wong (Top Chef). Korean-inspired brunch: kimchi fried rice w/ perfect soft egg. Reservations essential — expect waits regardless. Kaimuki.

name: The Pig and the Lady
description: Chef Andrew Le's creative Vietnamese fusion. Pho French dip sandwich (genius), larb, green papaya salad. Great cocktails. Chinatown anchor.
hours: Lunch Mon–Fri, Dinner Mon–Sat, Brunch Sat–Sun

name: Highway Inn
description: Family-owned since 1947. Most tourist-accessible traditional Hawaiian food. Lau lau, kalua pig, poi, ahi poke, oxtail soup. Walkable from Ward/Kaka'ako.

name: Matsumoto Shave Ice
description: North Shore icon since 1951. Lines move fast. Rainbow with ice cream + azuki beans. Cash only. In Haleiwa town — combine with North Shore drive.

name: Ted's Bakery
description: North Shore (Pupukea) famous for haupia (coconut) cream pie — $6–8/slice. Also malasadas, manapua, local plate lunches. Cash preferred.

name: Giovanni's Shrimp Truck
description: Original North Shore garlic shrimp truck. $16–17 plate (12 shrimp, 2 scoops rice). Card accepted now. Expect line. Several trucks — this is the famous white one.

name: Waiola Shave Ice
description: Kapahulu favorite. Fine ice, huge flavor selection. Get rainbow with ice cream + azuki beans. Walkable from Waikiki on Kapahulu crawl.

name: KCC Farmers Market (Saturday)
description: Best food experience in Honolulu. Saturday 7:30–11AM only. Prepared food stalls: poke, malasadas, banh mi, laulau, tropical fruit. Pair with Diamond Head sunrise hike.

name: Maunakea Marketplace
description: Indoor Chinatown food court. Filipino, Chinese, Vietnamese, Hawaiian stalls. Very cheap, very local. Excellent budget lunch.

name: Zippy's
description: Hawaii's beloved 24-hr local chain (like a diner). Chili + rice ($9–11), oxtail soup, malasadas. Multiple locations. Kapahulu one is 24/7.

name: Pearl Harbor Historic Sites
description: Full day (6–8 hrs). USS Arizona Memorial (FREE, reserve at recreation.gov), USS Bowfin Submarine, Battleship Missouri, Pacific Aviation Museum. Combo tickets save $.

name: Polynesian Cultural Center
description: 6 Polynesian villages, canoe pageant, Ali'i Luau, 'Ha: Breath of Life' evening show. Packages from $158 (Gateway) to $294 (Super Ambassador). Closed Sundays. On North Shore route.

name: Kualoa Ranch
description: 4,000-acre ranch on windward coast. Jurassic Park, Lost, Jumanji filming locations. ATV, zipline, horseback, movie site tours. Book specific tours well ahead.

name: Diamond Head State Monument
description: Iconic crater hike. 1.6 mi RT, 560 ft gain, 99 stairs + 74-step spiral staircase in WWII bunker. Panoramic Waikiki views. Reserve parking at gostateparks.hawaii.gov (30 days out).

name: Hanauma Bay Nature Preserve
description: BEST snorkeling on Oahu. $25 non-resident. Mandatory 9-min reef video. REEF-SAFE sunscreen only (zinc/titanium). Reservations open 2 days ahead at 6:58 AM HST — sells out in minutes. Closed Tuesdays.

name: Bishop Museum
description: Hawaii's premier museum of Pacific culture & natural history. 3 floors of Hawaiian Hall, royal regalia, featherwork, planetarium. Free parking. Allow 3–4 hrs.

name: Iolani Palace
description: Only royal palace on US soil. Home of King Kalakaua & Queen Lili'uokalani. Audio tour ~$30. Basement galleries: Crown Jewels, feather cloaks. Combine with Mission Houses & Kawaiahao Church.

name: Manoa Falls Trail
description: 1.6 mi RT to 150-ft waterfall through rainforest. ALWAYS muddy — wear waterproof shoes. $7 parking (cash) at Paradise Park. Mosquitoes intense — bring DEET. No swimming (leptospirosis).

name: Makapuu Lighthouse Trail
description: 2 mi RT paved trail, moderate incline. BEST whale watching (Nov–Apr). Panoramic ocean views, Molokai visible on clear days. No shade — go early or late. Free parking.

name: Lanikai Pillbox (Kaiwa Ridge)
address: Kaelepulu Dr / Mid Pacific Country Club
description: BEST free sunrise hike. ~1.6 mi RT to 2 WWII pillboxes on ridge. Sweeping Lanikai/Mokulua views. Street parking only (residential — be respectful). No facilities.

name: Koko Head Crater Trail
description: 1,048 railroad-tie stairs to summit. 1–1.5 hrs. No shade. 360° views: Honolulu, Hanauma Bay, crater. Popular with military/fitness crowd. Arrive before 7–8 AM.

name: Ho'omaluhia Botanical Garden
description: 400-acre garden backed by dramatic Ko'olau peaks. Iconic entrance road photo. Free admission. Free guided nature walks some mornings. No swimming in lake.

name: Nu'uanu Pali Lookout
description: Historic 1795 battle site (Kamehameha I unified Oahu). Sweeping windward views. $7/vehicle parking. Often very windy — secure hats. Sacred site — don't take rocks.

name: Shark's Cove (Pupukea)
description: North Shore's best summer snorkeling (May–Sep). Rocky entry, tide pools, abundant fish. Winter: big waves, no swimming. Water shoes essential. Parking fills early.

name: Byodo-In Temple
description: Non-practicing Buddhist temple in Valley of the Temples. Replica of 950-yr-old Japanese temple. Peaceful grounds, koi ponds, peacocks, meditation. $5 entry (cash).

name: Pu'u Ualaka'a (Tantalus Lookout)
address: Round Top Dr, off Makiki Heights Dr
description: Panoramic sunset/night view of Honolulu, Diamond Head, leeward coast from ~1,000 ft. Cool upland forest. Winding drive — go slow. Easy add-on to Makiki hike or dinner in town.

name: Waikiki Beach
description: Iconic, crowded, but convenient. Best swimming near Royal Hawaiian. Surf lessons, catamaran cruises, outrigger canoe. Parking: Kapiolani Park (free) or hotel $35–55/day.

name: Hanauma Bay
description: See Activities for snorkeling details. Inner reef calm; outer reef for confident swimmers. Tram $1–3 saves steep walk. Closed Tuesdays.

name: Kailua Beach Park
description: BEST overall beach — calm turquoise water, white sand, free parking (~100 spaces, fills by 9–10 AM weekends). Kayak/SUP rentals to Mokulua Islands. Lifeguards 9AM–5:30PM.

name: Lanikai Beach
description: Postcard-perfect. Street parking only (~30 spots, fills by 8 AM). Better: park at Kailua Beach, bike/walk 20 min. No facilities. Mokulua Islands kayak launch.

name: Ko Olina Lagoons
description: 4 man-made lagoons — calm year-round regardless of ocean. Great for kids/families. Free public parking at each lagoon (fills by mid-morning weekends). Disney Aulani here.

name: Waimea Bay
description: Summer: great swimming/snorkeling. Winter: 20–40 ft waves — SPECTATORS ONLY. Free large lot, restrooms, showers, lifeguards. Jump rock in summer (check depth).

name: Sandy Beach Park
description: World-class bodysurfing. CONSISTENTLY ranked Hawaii's most dangerous beach — powerful shore break causes spinal injuries. EXPERTS ONLY. Watch from sand.

name: Ala Moana Beach Park
description: Calm protected channel, local vibe, joggers, picnics. Less touristy than Waikiki. Next to Ala Moana Center for post-beach shopping/AC. Avoid after dark.

name: Sunset Beach
description: Winter: massive waves (Pipeline neighbor). Summer: flat, swimmable, great snorkeling. Free parking across street. Banzai Pipeline view point nearby.

name: Shark's Cove (Pupukea)
description: See Activities entry. Best summer snorkeling on North Shore. Rocky entry — water shoes required. Tide pools at low tide. Parking fills by 8–9 AM.
